beats.intro: Chapter fifty-eight. [[sub]]Even when a number isn't a perfect square, part of its square root can often come out of the radical.
beats.rule: The key fact: the square root of a product is the product of the square roots. [[ex]]For example, the square root of nine times four [[left]]is the square root of thirty-six, which is six. [[right]]And the square root of nine times the square root of four is three times two, also six. [[use]]So we can split a radical into factors, and simplify the ones that are perfect squares.
beats.eighteen: Simplify the square root of eighteen. [[ask]]Ask: what's the greatest perfect square that divides eighteen? Nine. [[split]]Write eighteen as nine times two. [[out]]The square root of nine is three, so three comes out in front. [[ans]]The square root of eighteen is three root two. [[read]]Read it as three root two: it means three times the square root of two. [[chk]]Check: three root two, squared, is nine times two, eighteen.
beats.pairs: When the perfect square isn't obvious, use prime factors. [[q]]Take the square root of seventy-two. [[tree]]Break seventy-two into primes: two, two, two, three, three. [[pair]]Under a square root, every pair of equal factors is a perfect square. [[out]]Each pair leaves the radical as a single factor: one two comes out, and one three comes out. [[left]]The unpaired two stays inside. [[ans]]So the square root of seventy-two is two times three, six, root two.
beats.great: Use the greatest perfect square factor, or you'll have to keep going. [[q]]For the square root of forty-eight, four is a perfect square factor: [[four]]that gives two root twelve. [[more]]But twelve still has a perfect square factor, four, so this isn't simplified yet. [[sixteen]]Using sixteen from the start gives four root three in one step. [[same]]Both paths end at four root three.
beats.q2: Quick check. Is it fully simplified?
beats.cube: Cube roots work the same way, with triples instead of pairs. [[q]]Simplify the cube root of forty. [[tree]]Forty is two times two times two times five. [[trip]]Under a cube root, three equal factors make a perfect cube. [[out]]The triple of twos comes out as one two. [[ans]]So the cube root of forty is two times the cube root of five. [[neg]]Negatives are fine with cube roots: the cube root of negative one hundred twenty-eight is negative four times the cube root of two.
beats.q3: Quick check. Simplify the cube root.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]The square root of a product is the product of the square roots. [[w2]]Pull out the greatest perfect square factor, or pull out one factor for every pair of primes. [[w3]]For cube roots, pull out one factor for every triple. [[w4]]A radical is simplified when nothing more can come out. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final1: Chapter practice. Simplify the square roots.

beats.finish: Nice work. That's the end of chapter fifty-eight, simplifying radicals.
